title: Spin textures at the Fermi surface of ferromagnets and associated torque
authors: T. Valet, J. Li, H. Jaffrès, V. Cros, M. Chshiev, R. Raimondi
abstract: We establish theoretically that transverse spin textures are generically induced by the spin-orbit interaction at the Fermi surface of centrosymmetric ferromagnetic metals. We confirm this prediction with {\em ab initio} computations for Fe, Co and Ni. By symmetry, this cannot be associated with spin-orbit torques under a uniform current. However, a new {\em current-gradient-induced} torque emerges in nanoscale geometries. For a series of Ni-based bilayers, the computed Ni thickness dependence of the current-gradient-induced torque is in quantitative agreement with measurements previously attributed to orbital torques. We discuss how this opens a new avenue for the electrical control of magnetic orders, possibly also including the Néel vector of metallic altermagnets.
summary: This work theoretically predicts that spin-orbit interaction induces transverse spin textures on the Fermi surface of ferromagnetic metals. These textures give rise to a novel current-gradient-induced spin-orbit torque, which the authors demonstrate quantitatively matches experimental measurements in Ni bilayers. This suggests a new mechanism for electrically controlling magnetic properties beyond traditional orbital torque explanations.
main_problem: The paper theoretically establishes the existence of transverse spin textures at the Fermi surface of centrosymmetric ferromagnets and predicts a novel current-gradient-induced spin-orbit torque (SOT) associated with these textures.
main_result: The predicted current-gradient-induced SOT quantitatively accounts for measurements previously attributed to orbital torques in Ni-based bilayers, opening a new avenue for electrical control of magnetic order.
method: The study combines analytic derivations using a two-band approximation with ab initio computations (VASP) to calculate spin polarization and torque components.
model_or_system: The system involves centrosymmetric ferromagnetic metals (Fe, Co, Ni) analyzed via their spin-orbit interaction (SOI) effects on the Fermi surface, modeled using quantum kinetic theory and a two-band approach.
key_observables: Transverse spin texture ($s^\perp$), current-gradient-induced torque ($	au^E_{ib}$), and the thickness dependence of the damping-like torque efficiency ($\xi_{E}^{DL}$).
important_parameters: Fermi level crossing points, SOI strength (gaps of 20–60 meV), and film thickness ($t$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on a two-band approximation and assumes the top interface acts as a diffusive bottom boundary when solving the Boltzmann equation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the spin mosaics and resulting transverse spin textures on the Fermi surfaces (Fig. 1, 2), and show the current density profiles and thickness dependence of the torque components in Ni films (Fig. 3, 4).
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the theoretical origin of transverse spin textures via SOI to deriving the current-gradient-induced torque, and finally validating this torque by comparing theoretical predictions with experimental measurements on Ni-based bilayers.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter magnetism, the derivation of novel, symmetry-protected torques and the use of quantum kinetic theory to link electronic structure (Fermi surface topology) to macroscopic transport phenomena are relevant to understanding non-equilibrium quantum dynamics.
